images.title: A diagonal makes two triangles, 360° in all
images.purpose: Shows quadrilateral SOME split by diagonal SM into two triangles, with angles 75°, 95°, 110° and 80° adding up to 360°.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large quadrilateral in the centre, split by one diagonal into two lightly shaded triangles, with its four angles marked and one sum under the shape.
images.exact_structure: One convex irregular quadrilateral SOME in dark outline, no sides parallel, with S at the left, O at the top, M at the right and E at the bottom. The diagonal SM is a dashed dark line from S to M. The top triangle SOM is lightly filled teal (#0072B2) and the bottom triangle SEM is lightly filled amber (#E69F00). Each corner has one small reddish purple (#CC79A7) arc inside the shape: 75° at S, 95° at O, 110° at M and 80° at E. Under the shape, centred, the line 180° + 180° = 360°. No corner letters are shown. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Any quadrilateral splits into two triangles, so its four angles add up to 360°.
images.description: Shows quadrilateral SOME split by diagonal SM into two triangles, with angles 75°, 95°, 110° and 80° adding up to 360°.

image_decisions.why: Two shaded triangles inside one quadrilateral show where the 360° comes from, with the example's own angles.
